previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after presenting with bright red blood per rectum, right-sided abdominal pain, and ongoing lightheadedness. She had recently undergone perineal rectosigmoidectomy for rectal prolapse. Imaging revealed an 8.5-cm perirectal fluid collection concerning for abscess and anastomotic leak. She underwent interventional radiology-guided drainage of the collection and was started on intravenous Ciprofloxacin and Metronidazole. Cultures grew pan-sensitive E. coli and Bacteroides fragilis. She developed significant constipation post-drainage, with no bowel movements despite laxatives and enemas. After two doses of intravenous neostigmine, she had multiple bowel movements, with radiographic improvement. A cracked drain tube required replacement on hospital day 10. The drain was removed when output became minimal, and she was discharged home on oral antibiotics and a bowel regimen with home health services arranged. She remained stable throughout with no cardiac or respiratory complications.
